# Bhaddākāpilānītherīgāthā (Thig 4.1)

**ID:** Thig 4.1
**Section:** Therīgāthā (thig)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Bhaddākāpilānītherīgāthā
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/thig4.1

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bhaddākāpilānītherīgāthā* (Thig 4.1) comprises the four verses (verses 63–66) attributed to the elder nun Bhaddā Kāpilānī in the *Catukkanipāta* of the *Therīgāthā* [SuttaCentral; Skilling; Collett 2014]. In the poem, verse 65 explicitly proclaims her attainment of the three higher knowledges (*tevijjā*), implicitly indicating her mastery of the recollection of past lives [Collett 2014]. The exegesis of these stanzas is preserved in Dhammapāla's *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (pp. 66–74) [Skilling], which shares extensive textual material with the verses [DharmaNexus]. Modern English translations of the text have been produced by Bhikkhu Sujato and Ayya Soma [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral records resembling parallels to these verses in multiple early Buddhist texts, notably Dhammapada 423, the *Tikaṇṇasutta* (AN 3.58), *Jāṇussoṇisutta* (AN 3.59), *Tevijja Sutta* (Iti 99), *Brahmāyu Sutta* (MN 91), *Vāseṭṭha Sutta* (MN 98; Snp 3.9), and two discourses of the Saṃyutta Nikāya (SN 7.8, SN 7.13) [SuttaCentral]. Beyond Pali, resembling stanzas appear in Chinese translations of the *Dharmapada* and *Udānavarga* collections (T 210, T 212, T 213), the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G-Dhp 1–50), and Sanskrit as well as Tibetan *Udānavarga* witnesses (UV 33, UVS 33, D4099, D0326) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within Pali literature, DharmaNexus detects near-verbatim text reuse between the four verses of this text (§1.1–4.4) and the *Bhaddākāpilānītherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 27, §64.1–67.4), along with multiple matches in the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
